issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order differs between the problem statement/solution and the template. The UML and solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) but the template defines Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch will confuse students and cause compilation or usage errors (e.g., example code in Main expects the (String, String[]) order).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor to match the specification and solution: declare it as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and adjust parameter usage accordingly so examples in Main and the UML align with the template.

issues.description: Constructor signature for Meal is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement's UML and the solution both specify Meal(String, String[]) (name first, then ingredients), but the template implementation declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first). This mismatch breaks the example usage in Main (which calls new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})) and creates confusion for students mapping the problem specification to the starter code and expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Meal constructor to match the problem statement and solution: declare it as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and assign fields accordingly (this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients). This aligns the starter code with the UML, Main usage, and the reference solution.
